peripheral_nerve: Spinal accessory (CN XI) + C3–4 cervical plexus
clinical_emg_pearl: Lateral winging; injured in posterior triangle (e.g., node biopsy).
needle_position: Prone. Upper: neutral. Middle: arm abducted 90° with elbow bent over the table edge. Lower: arm overhead.
needle_site: Upper: at the angle between neck and shoulder. Middle: halfway from the middle of the scapular spine to the spinous process at that level. Lower: two fingerbreadths lateral to the spinous process level with the inferior scapular angle.
needle_activation: Upper: shrug. Middle: lift the abducted arm off the table. Lower: lift the overhead arm off the table.
needle_off_target: Upper too deep → levator scapulae. Middle too deep → rhomboids. Lower too deep or low → latissimus dorsi.

clinical_emg_pearl: Shares dorsal scapular nerve with rhomboids.
verification: Nerve verified; roots by anatomic convention
needle_site: Two fingerbreadths above and one fingerbreadth medial to the superior (medial) angle of the scapula, passing through upper trapezius.
needle_activation: Elevate the scapula.
needle_off_target: Too shallow → trapezius. Too deep → paraspinals.

bedside_test: Scapular retraction (hand on hip, push elbow back)
clinical_emg_pearl: Branch comes off the root: rhomboid denervation points to C5 root, not upper trunk.
verification_note: MRC lists C4, C5; US EMG texts usually list C5 (C4–5).
needle_position: Prone, dorsum of the hand resting on the small of the back.
needle_site: Major: just medial to the vertebral border, halfway between the scapular spine and the inferior angle (through middle trapezius). Minor: one fingerbreadth medial to where the scapular spine meets the vertebral border.
needle_activation: Lift the hand off the small of the back.
needle_off_target: Too shallow → trapezius. Too deep → erector spinae (major) or serratus posterior superior (minor).

clinical_emg_pearl: Branch comes off the root: helps separate root from plexus. Medial winging. Parsonage-Turner often involves it.
needle_position: Prone, arm hanging off the table edge.
needle_site: Just lateral to the inferior angle of the scapula.
needle_activation: Push the hand forward against resistance.
needle_off_target: Too shallow → latissimus dorsi. Too high → teres major.
needle_note: Stay over a rib; the pleura lies just deep to the intercostal space.

clinical_emg_pearl: Upper-trunk branch; mostly board-trivia.
verification: Nerve verified; roots by anatomic convention

clinical_emg_pearl: Upper-trunk branch. Entrapment at suprascapular notch hits both supra- and infraspinatus.
needle_position: Prone, arm abducted 90° with elbow bent over the table edge.
needle_site: In the supraspinous fossa just above the middle of the scapular spine, through middle trapezius.
needle_activation: Externally rotate the arm.
needle_off_target: Too shallow → trapezius.

clinical_emg_pearl: Isolated involvement suggests a lesion at the spinoglenoid notch (e.g., ganglion cyst).
needle_position: Prone, arm abducted 90° with elbow bent over the table edge.
needle_site: In the infraspinous fossa, two fingerbreadths below the medial part of the scapular spine.
needle_activation: Externally rotate the arm.
needle_off_target: Too shallow → trapezius. Too lateral → posterior deltoid.

needle_site: Into the anterior axillary fold (aim toward the clavicular fibres).
needle_activation: Bring the arm across the chest (horizontal adduction).
needle_off_target: Too deep → coracobrachialis. Too lateral → biceps.
needle_note: Perotto describes one site for the whole muscle.

clinical_emg_pearl: Medial pectoral input makes it useful in lower-trunk/medial-cord plexopathy.
verification_note: MRC lists C6–8; Gray's-tradition texts list C7–T1 via the medial pectoral nerve.
needle_site: Into the anterior axillary fold (aim toward the lower, sternocostal fibres).
needle_activation: Bring the arm across the chest (horizontal adduction).
needle_off_target: Too deep → coracobrachialis. Too lateral → biceps.
needle_note: Perotto describes one site for the whole muscle.

clinical_emg_pearl: Pec minor syndrome: neurogenic TOS mimic.
verification: Nerve verified; roots by anatomic convention
needle_site: In the midclavicular line, advance through pectoralis major onto the front of the 3rd rib, then pull back slightly.
needle_activation: Depress the scapula.
needle_off_target: Too shallow → pectoralis major.
needle_note: Keep the needle on the rib to avoid the pleura.

bedside_test: Adduct and extend arm (cough test palpation)
clinical_emg_pearl: Posterior-cord branch above the radial nerve: abnormal lat + triceps points to posterior cord or C7.
needle_position: Prone, arm at the side, palm up.
needle_site: Three fingerbreadths below the posterior axillary fold, along the fold.
needle_activation: Extend, adduct and internally rotate the arm.
needle_off_target: Too medial → teres major.

verification_note: MRC lists C5–7; Gray's-tradition texts list C5–6.
needle_position: Prone, arm abducted 90° with elbow bent over the table edge.
needle_site: Along the lateral border of the scapula, three fingerbreadths above the inferior angle.
needle_activation: Internally rotate the arm.
needle_off_target: Too low → serratus anterior. Too lateral → latissimus dorsi.

verification: Nerve verified; roots by anatomic convention

clinical_emg_pearl: Main C5 screening muscle. Axillary nerve injury from shoulder dislocation or surgical neck fracture; quadrilateral space.
verification_note: All texts agree on C5–6. Cadaveric fibre counts (Thimjon 2022, 40 sides) found C6, not C5, the larger contributor on 35% of sides vs C5 on 16%. EMG series (Levin) still behave as C5-predominant.
needle_position: Supine, arm at the side (middle deltoid).
needle_site: Middle deltoid: halfway between the acromion tip and the deltoid tubercle.
needle_activation: Abduct the arm.
needle_off_target: No significant pitfall listed.
needle_note: A history of repeated intramuscular injections here can confound findings. Anterior and posterior deltoid sites: pp. 104, 108.

clinical_emg_pearl: Spared or involved separately in quadrilateral space syndrome.
verification: Nerve verified; roots by anatomic convention
verification_note: MRC lists teres minor under axillary nerve but gives no root values.
needle_position: Prone, arm abducted 90° with elbow bent over the table edge.
needle_site: Along the lateral scapular border, one-third of the way from the acromion down to the inferior angle.
needle_activation: Externally rotate the arm.
needle_off_target: Too high → supraspinatus. Too low → teres major. Too medial → infraspinatus. Too shallow → trapezius.

clinical_emg_pearl: MC nerve pierces it; a lesion distal to it spares coracobrachialis.
verification: Nerve verified; roots by anatomic convention
needle_site: On the front of the arm, four fingerbreadths below the coracoid; go to bone, then pull back.
needle_activation: With the elbow bent 90°, lift the arm forward.
needle_off_target: Too shallow → biceps or anterior deltoid. Too lateral → brachialis.

surgical_emg_evidence: Levin 1996: abnormal in 5/7 C5 and 4/9 C6
clinical_emg_pearl: Biceps reflex C5–6. Biceps + deltoid together = C5/6 root or upper trunk; add rhomboid/serratus/paraspinals to separate them.
needle_site: Into the muscle belly at mid-arm.
needle_activation: Flex the elbow or supinate the forearm.
needle_off_target: Too deep → brachialis.
needle_note: Recording site for musculocutaneous motor conduction studies.

clinical_emg_pearl: Dual innervation: lateral part from the radial nerve.
verification_note: Loyola agrees on dual MC + radial (C7) supply.
needle_site: Two fingerbreadths above the elbow crease, just lateral to the biceps tendon and belly.
needle_activation: Bend the elbow with the forearm pronated, against light resistance only (heavy resistance recruits biceps).
needle_off_target: Too medial → biceps.

clinical_emg_pearl: Main C7 muscle (with FCR and pronator teres). Triceps reflex C7. Spared in spiral groove radial neuropathy (branches arise proximal).
verification_note: Perotto lists C7–T1 for the lateral head (C7, C8 emphasized).
needle_site: Lateral head: just behind the deltoid insertion (deltoid tubercle).
needle_activation: Extend the elbow.
needle_off_target: Too anterior or too proximal → deltoid.
needle_note: Branches leave the radial nerve high, so the triceps is usually spared in spiral-groove (Saturday night) palsy. Perotto also describes long- and medial-head sites (pp. 99–101).

peripheral_nerve: Radial (nerve to anconeus via medial head of triceps branch)
clinical_emg_pearl: Easy to needle; branch arises in the spiral groove region.
verification_note: Loyola lists radial nerve with C5–T1 (the whole nerve); most texts give C7–8. PM&R Recap lists C6–8; the app uses Recap as the primary value and accepts C7–8.
needle_site: Lay the little finger on the olecranon and the next two fingers along the ulna; insert just past the middle fingertip, on the radial side of the ulna.
needle_activation: Extend the elbow.
needle_off_target: Too radial → ECU. Too deep → supinator.

clinical_emg_pearl: Radial branch above the elbow. Brachioradialis (supinator) reflex C5–6. First muscle to check in spiral groove palsy (involved).
verification_note: MRC lists C5–6; many EMG references give C6 (C5–6) as the key root; Levin data show strong C5 involvement.
needle_site: On the elbow crease, halfway between the biceps tendon and the lateral epicondyle; about 1.3 cm (½ inch) deep.
needle_activation: Bend the elbow with the forearm in neutral (thumb up).
needle_off_target: Too lateral → ECRL.

clinical_emg_pearl: Arises above the PIN, so it's preserved in PIN palsy: radial wrist deviation on extension.
verification_note: MRC lists C5–6; Gray's-tradition and EMG texts often list C6–7. PM&R Recap lists C6–7; the app uses Recap as the primary value and accepts C5–6.
needle_site: Two fingerbreadths below the lateral epicondyle (Perotto gives one site for ECRL and ECRB together).
needle_activation: Extend the wrist toward the radial side.
needle_off_target: No pitfall listed. Perotto notes ECRL and ECRB cannot be reliably separated with a needle.

peripheral_nerve: Radial (deep branch, usually before the arcade of Frohse)
verification_note: Not in MRC. Gray's-tradition texts list C7–8; many clinical charts list C6–7.
needle_site: Two fingerbreadths below the lateral epicondyle (same site as ECRL).
needle_activation: Extend the wrist toward the radial side.
needle_off_target: No pitfall listed. Perotto notes ECRL and ECRB cannot be reliably separated with a needle.

clinical_emg_pearl: PIN passes through it (arcade of Frohse). Often partly spared in PIN syndrome because its branches arise proximally.
verification_note: MRC lists C6–7; Gray's-tradition texts list C5–6 (C6 main).
needle_site: Just radial to the distal end of the biceps tendon insertion, passing through extensor digitorum.
needle_activation: Supinate the forearm.
needle_off_target: Too lateral → brachioradialis. Watch for the radial artery.

clinical_emg_pearl: Finger drop with preserved wrist extension = PIN.
needle_site: At the junction of the upper and middle thirds of the forearm, halfway between the radius and ulna. About 1.3 cm (½ inch) deep.
needle_activation: Extend the fingers at the MCP joints.
needle_off_target: Too deep → EPL. Too far toward the radius → ECRB. Too far toward the ulna → ECU.
needle_note: Involved in PIN and more proximal radial lesions.

verification: Nerve verified; roots by anatomic convention
needle_site: On the ulnar edge of the extensor digitorum site (upper–middle third junction, between radius and ulna).
needle_activation: Extend the little finger.
needle_off_target: Too radial → extensor digitorum. Too ulnar → ECU.
needle_note: Perotto treats it with extensor digitorum; it often blends with that muscle.

needle_site: Mid-forearm, just over (dorsal to) the shaft of the ulna.
needle_activation: Extend the wrist toward the ulnar side.
needle_off_target: Too radial → EPL. Too proximal → anconeus.

bedside_test: Thumb abduction in plane of palm
needle_site: Over the radius at mid-forearm, passing through extensor digitorum.
needle_activation: Abduct the thumb in the plane of the palm (radial abduction).
needle_off_target: Too proximal → ECRB. Too distal → EPB. Too ulnar → extensor digitorum.

needle_site: On the ulnar side of the radius, four fingerbreadths above the wrist, through extensor digitorum.
needle_activation: Extend the thumb at the MCP joint.
needle_off_target: Too proximal → APL.

bedside_test: Thumb IP extension (lift thumb off table)
needle_site: Mid-forearm along the radial border of the ulna, passing through ECU.
needle_activation: Extend the thumb tip (IP joint).
needle_off_target: Too ulnar → extensor digitorum. Too proximal → APL.

bedside_test: Index MCP extension with fist made
clinical_emg_pearl: Key EMG muscle: a C8 radial muscle. Abnormal EIP + FDI argues C8 root or lower trunk, not ulnar neuropathy.
needle_site: Two fingerbreadths proximal to the ulnar styloid, just radial to the ulna. About 1.3 cm (½ inch) deep.
needle_activation: Point the index finger with the other fingers curled into a fist.
needle_off_target: Too radial → APL. Too proximal → extensor digitorum.
needle_note: Typically the last muscle the radial nerve reaches. Used as the recording site for radial motor conduction studies.

surgical_emg_evidence: Levin 1996: abnormal in 7/9 C6 and 17/28 C7
clinical_emg_pearl: Best muscle for C6 in Levin's data. Usually spared in carpal tunnel syndrome and AIN; involved in proximal median lesions.
needle_site: Find the midpoint between the medial epicondyle and the biceps tendon, then go 2 fingerbreadths distal.
needle_activation: Pronate the forearm.
needle_off_target: Too deep → FDS. Too ulnar → FCR.
needle_note: Usually the first muscle the median nerve supplies. Can be spared in pronator syndrome if its branch arises above the compression.

clinical_emg_pearl: Core C7 screening muscle alongside triceps.
verification_note: Perotto adds C8 (C6–8, C7 emphasized).
needle_site: Find the midpoint between the medial epicondyle and the biceps tendon, then go 3–4 fingerbreadths distal.
needle_activation: Flex the wrist toward the radial side.
needle_off_target: Too deep → FDS, then FPL. Too lateral → pronator teres. Too medial → palmaris longus.
needle_note: At the wrist, the median nerve runs just ulnar to the FCR tendon.

clinical_emg_pearl: Absent in ~15%.
verification: Nerve verified; roots by anatomic convention
needle_site: On a line from the medial epicondyle to the middle of the volar wrist, at the junction of its upper and middle thirds.
needle_activation: Cup the palm.
needle_off_target: Too medial → FCU. Too radial → FCR. Too deep → FDS.

verification_note: MRC lists C7–T1; Gray's-tradition texts list C8–T1. PM&R Recap lists C7–8; the app uses Recap as the primary value and accepts C7–T1.
needle_site: Rest your palm on the patient's volar wrist and point your index finger toward the biceps tendon; enter just ulnar to your fingertip, through palmaris longus.
needle_activation: Flex one finger at the PIP joint while the other fingers are held straight.
needle_off_target: Too radial → FCR. Too ulnar → FDP.

clinical_emg_pearl: AIN syndrome: weak 'OK' sign, no sensory loss.
verification_note: MRC lists C7–8; Gray's-tradition sources (e.g., AIN entries) list C8–T1. PM&R Recap lists C7–T1; the app uses Recap as the primary value and accepts C7–8, C8–T1.
needle_site: Little finger on the olecranon, other fingers along the ulna; enter just past the index fingertip, just ulnar to the shaft. The median (AIN) part lies deeper, about 3–5 cm.
needle_activation: Flex the index-finger DIP joint.
needle_off_target: Too volar → FCU. Shallower (1–2 cm) lands in the ulnar part of FDP.

clinical_emg_pearl: Key AIN muscle. Abnormal FPL + normal median sensory nerve conductions = AIN or C8/lower trunk; check APB/FDI.
verification_note: MRC lists C7–8; IMAIOS/Gray's-derived sources list C8–T1. PM&R Recap lists C7–T1; the app uses Recap as the primary value and accepts C7–8, C8–T1.
needle_site: Mid-forearm, entering from the radial side just volar to the radius, through FCR and FDS.
needle_activation: Flex the thumb tip (IP joint).
needle_off_target: Too shallow → FDS.

clinical_emg_pearl: Needle from dorsal approach through interosseous membrane.
verification_note: Not in MRC; root values follow AIN (C7–8 vs C8–T1 by source). PM&R Recap lists C7–T1; the app uses Recap as the primary value and accepts C7–8, C8–T1.
needle_site: Three fingerbreadths above the midpoint between the radial and ulnar styloids; pass through the interosseous membrane, about 2 cm (¾ inch) deep.
needle_activation: Pronate the forearm.
needle_off_target: Too deep → FDS.

clinical_emg_pearl: Often spared in ulnar neuropathy at the elbow (fascicular sparing or branches above the elbow), so sparing doesn't localize.
verification_note: MRC lists C7–T1; Gray's-tradition texts list C7–8 (T1). PM&R Recap lists C8–T1; the app uses Recap as the primary value and accepts C7–T1.
needle_site: Two fingerbreadths volar to the ulna, at the junction of the upper and middle thirds of the forearm.
needle_activation: Flex the wrist toward the ulnar side.
needle_off_target: Too deep → FDP.

clinical_emg_pearl: Involved in elbow lesions, spared at Guyon's canal (useful for localization).
verification_note: MRC lists C7–8; Gray's-tradition texts list C8–T1. PM&R Recap lists C7–T1; the app uses Recap as the primary value and accepts C7–8, C8–T1.
needle_site: Same entry as above (past the index fingertip, just ulnar to the ulnar shaft), but shallow: the ulnar part lies about 1–2 cm deep.
needle_activation: Flex the little-finger DIP joint.
needle_off_target: Too volar → FCU. Deeper lands in the median (AIN) part.

clinical_emg_pearl: Recording muscle for median motor NCS. True neurogenic TOS: APB wasting > ADM (Gilliatt-Sumner hand).
needle_site: Halfway along a line from the thumb MCP joint (volar side) to the first CMC joint. Shallow: about 0.6–1.3 cm (¼–½ inch).
needle_activation: Lift the thumb straight up off the palm (palmar abduction).
needle_off_target: Too deep → opponens pollicis.
needle_note: The thenar muscle closest to the skin. Involved in median lesions at any level except isolated AIN.

needle_site: Halfway between the CMC and MCP joints of the thumb on the radial side, sliding between APB and the 1st metacarpal; about 1.3–2 cm deep.
needle_activation: Touch the thumb to the little finger.
needle_off_target: Too deep → adductor pollicis. Too medial → APB.

clinical_emg_pearl: Deep head is ulnar; variable dual supply.
needle_site: On a line from the ulnar side of the thumb MCP joint to the pisiform, one-third of the way from the thumb end; about 0.6–1.3 cm deep.
needle_activation: Flex the thumb MCP joint.
needle_off_target: Too deep → opponens pollicis, then adductor pollicis.

clinical_emg_pearl: Second lumbrical vs interosseous comparison (lumbrical–interossei distal latency study) in CTS.
needle_site: In the palm just proximal to the MCP joint, on the radial side of the flexor tendon (lumbrical number = MCP joint number minus one).
needle_activation: Keep the MCP joints straight and extend the IP joints against resistance.
needle_off_target: 1st too deep → adductor pollicis, then 1st dorsal interosseous. 2nd too deep → adductor pollicis or 2nd dorsal interosseous.
needle_note: The proximal palmar crease overlies the 2nd MCP joint; the distal crease overlies the 3rd–5th.

clinical_emg_pearl: Superficial-branch muscle: spared in deep palmar branch lesions.
verification: Nerve verified; roots by anatomic convention
needle_site: Ulnar edge of the hand about 5 cm (2 inches) from the proximal palmar crease; enter at about 30° to the skin and go only about 0.6 cm deep.
needle_activation: Press on the pisiform (reflex activation) or resist little-finger abduction.
needle_off_target: Too deep → abductor or opponens digiti minimi.

clinical_emg_pearl: Recording muscle for ulnar motor NCS (stimulate wrist, below elbow, above elbow).
needle_site: Halfway between the ulnar side of the 5th MCP joint and the pisiform; about 0.6–1.3 cm deep.
needle_activation: Abduct the little finger.
needle_off_target: Too deep → opponens digiti minimi.

needle_site: Halfway between the pisiform and the palmar base of the little finger's proximal phalanx.
needle_activation: Flex the little finger at the MCP joint.
needle_off_target: Too deep → opponens digiti minimi (touching bone means pull back).

clinical_emg_pearl: MRC groups this with the hypothenar muscles.
needle_site: Halfway between the radial side of the 5th MCP joint and the radial side of the pisiform.
needle_activation: Bring the little finger toward the thumb.
needle_off_target: Too deep → 4th lumbrical, then 3rd palmar interosseous.

clinical_emg_pearl: Weakness gives claw of ring/little fingers.
needle_site: In the palm just proximal to the MCP joint, on the radial side of the flexor tendon.
needle_activation: Keep the MCP joints straight and extend the IP joints against resistance.
needle_off_target: 3rd too deep → 2nd palmar interosseous. 4th too deep → opponens digiti minimi, then 3rd palmar interosseous.

surgical_emg_evidence: Levin 1996: FDI abnormal in 6/6 C8 radiculopathies
clinical_emg_pearl: FDI is the most-needled ulnar hand muscle and a recording site for ulnar NCS (deep branch / Guyon's canal).
needle_site: FDI: on a line across the hand at the level of the thumb MCP joint, just radial to the 2nd metacarpal. The 2nd–4th dorsal interossei sit at the same level: radial to the 3rd metacarpal, then ulnar to the 3rd and 4th.
needle_activation: FDI: move the index finger toward the thumb (radial abduction).
needle_off_target: FDI too deep → adductor pollicis.
needle_note: The dorsal and volar interossei divide the interosseous space obliquely rather than lying one above the other, so needle angle in the radial–ulnar direction matters more than depth. Innervation varies (occasional median supply).

needle_site: On the line across the hand at the level of the thumb MCP joint, about 0.6 cm deep: 1st just ulnar to the 2nd metacarpal, 2nd just radial to the 4th, 3rd just radial to the 5th.
needle_activation: Move the finger toward the middle finger (adduction).
needle_off_target: Too shallow → the neighboring dorsal interosseous. Too deep (1st) → adductor pollicis.

clinical_emg_pearl: Froment sign: FPL (median/AIN) substitutes for adductor pollicis.
needle_position: Hand relaxed, palm down or neutral.
needle_site: Enter at the free edge of the first web space, aiming toward the base of the first metacarpal.
needle_activation: Pull the thumb in against the index finger.
needle_off_target: Too dorsal → first dorsal interosseous. Too volar → opponens pollicis.
needle_note: The last muscle the ulnar nerve reaches.

clinical_emg_pearl: MRC lists FPB under both median and ulnar.
needle_site: Same point as the superficial head, deeper: about 1.3–2 cm.
needle_activation: Flex the thumb MCP joint.
needle_off_target: Too deep → adductor pollicis.

surgical_emg_evidence: Levin 1996: paraspinal abnormalities in only 8/26 C7 cases
clinical_emg_pearl: Abnormal paraspinals place the lesion at the root (proximal to the plexus). Normal paraspinals do not rule out radiculopathy, and their level is imprecise because of overlap.
verification_note: Dorsal-ramus innervation is standard across all sources; Levin data show low sensitivity.
needle_position: Prone, pillow under the chest so the neck flexes and the forehead rests on the table.
needle_site: Count from the C7 spinous process. Enter 1–2 fingerbreadths lateral to the spinous process and advance down to the lamina (multifidus lies in the angle between lamina and spinous process).
needle_activation: Lift or extend the head. If the muscle won't relax, have the patient press the head into the table.
needle_off_target: Too superficial → trapezius, rhomboids or splenius.
needle_note: Innervation overlaps one or two segments above and below, so level localization is imprecise. Near C7–T1, avoid going too deep: the author reports a case of unilateral Horner's syndrome.
